title: Joe Oliver's mutes, plunger and derby demonstration
summary: Dominique and Russell handle mutes on the table: long silver, con mute, plunger, tin can and derby hat effects Oliver used.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Did Joe use a mute very much? Yeah.
Very much.
What kind of a mute did he use?
A little silver mute. A little, uh. Long silver mute.
A long silver mute.
Yeah. He used that quite a bit. Because it was easier to blow than this short mute here. You see? The short mute here. It's kind of a strainer. He used a short mute like this. A con mute. Yeah.
A little con. Yeah. A little light bulb. You have one of those con mutes here too. Yeah.
You see? He used that to use his plunger. Then he used this. This is a light mute.

Oh, he put in this con mute. Yeah. The brass, started brass one. You see? I'll just show you. I'll never know. It's blown. It's blown. Yeah. I'm not blowing it. So you can blow it easy and I'll turn it down if you like.
No.
I just want to show you. Go ahead.
I just want to show you.
Yeah. That won't. That'll be good to have it on the table actually. I'll turn it down a little bit if you blow it. And then stick that little mute in and then use the plunger. Mm-hmm.
See? That's what he used. And Joe used to make high notes with those. It's just plunging. But it's hard.
This is harder than this one. Yeah, that con nude. That con nude is supposed to be a hard one to go.
It is. Because you can see the different tone with this nude and that nude. Excuse me? Excuse me? That's a long silver.
Long silver. Yeah. D&D&D D&D D& D&D D& D&D D& D&D D&
Think about it. When we used to take a tin can and hang it on that.
Oh yeah.
On our horn with a piece of wire on it.
Just a wire and hang it on an ordinary tin can.
Yeah, a tin can. And hang it on there. That's what it sounds like.
Yeah.
Same thing. See? Yeah. It sounds just like that tin you put on your horn.
Did Joe ever use a derby hat?
Yeah. Use a derby hat. He hold it long ways. Like that. Yeah. We all use it. See? Hold your belt there.
Hold the belt and a couple of fingers around. Yeah. And blow it. Blow right in that derby.
If you want to make a better effect on a derby, you put your derby, half of your horn out.
Well, half the horn open and half...
Half in the derby.
Half in the derby.
Beautiful. Yeah. That's how we use it. Better for the use derby over there.
